title: Study G: second blinded diagnosis, on the detection boundary (human versus committed rule)
purpose: Study E validated the human-plus-instrument workflow at ceiling on a corpus designed to be diagnosable. Study F mapped the instrument's detection boundary with a mechanical rule and found the rule fails exactly where evidence is entangled or borderline. Study G tests, blinded and pre-registered, whether a human reader with the full trace evidence outperforms the committed mechanical rule precisely in that regime.
diagnostician: Sadia Afrin Purba (Researcher B of Study E). She is unblinded to Study E's answer key but has never seen any Study G run, the Study G assignment, or this corpus's composition. Reusing a rater across independently blinded corpora is standard practice; her prior calibration on clear cases is part of what is being measured.

corpus.generators: the byte-identical Study E generators (via the Study F dispatch, commit 5c25350), simulator-only
corpus.composition_disclosure: Runs may express zero, one, or two failure mechanisms, at planted strengths ranging from physically absent to strongly expressed. The class balance, per-arm composition, knob levels, seeds, and generation order are WITHHELD from the diagnostician and from this public document; the full run-level assignment is committed below by SHA-256 and is revealed, with the answer key, only at unsealing.
corpus.generation_order: shuffled under a private draw, so trace timestamps carry no arm information
corpus.blinding: tools/blind_corpus.py blind (verbatim copy under random identifiers, leakage audit, SHA-256 answer-key commitment published before diagnosis begins), exactly as in Study E

comparator_rule.definition: the frozen mechanical decision rule of Study F (study_f_protocol.json, commit 5c25350), applied unchanged: analyzer-status flags, precedence noise > barren > shot, healthy iff no flag
comparator_rule.procedure: the rule's outputs on the blinded corpus are computed and hash-committed BEFORE the diagnostician receives the corpus, so neither the rule nor its outputs can react to her sheet

diagnostician_task: For each blinded run: one primary label from {healthy, barren_plateau, shot_starved, noise_dominated}, an optional secondary label, a confidence in [0,1], and free-text notes, using only the instrument's outputs on the trace. The class balance is not disclosed. 'Healthy' is the correct answer whenever the evidence does not support any failure mechanism.

primary.name: paired human-versus-rule primary-label comparison
primary.definition: For every run, the human's primary label and the rule's primary label are each scored correct/incorrect against the planted ground truth (for two-mechanism runs, either planted mechanism counts as a correct primary; order is not scored here). The registered primary outcome is the one-sided exact McNemar test on the discordant pairs (H1: the human is correct on more discordant runs than the rule).
primary.rationale: In the transition region the knob-defined label and the evidence genuinely diverge, so absolute accuracy is partly ill-defined there; both graders face the identical ambiguity on the identical runs, and the paired comparison cancels it. Runs where both are right or both are wrong do not enter the test.

secondary: per-arm detection-rate curves by planted strength level, human overlaid on rule (the psychometric overlay)

H2 (falsifiable): the human recovers the specific rule failure classes identified in Study F -- borderline-SNR runs graded 'Marginal' rather than 'Dominated', and shallow converged trajectories that mimic plateau variance -- at a higher rate than the rule
two-mechanism completeness: per-mechanism recall of the human flag set {primary, secondary} versus the rule flag set against the planted flags
false positives on mechanism-free runs, reported separately for the shallow converged-trajectory traps
H3: the human's reported confidence is lower inside the transition regions of Study F than on strongly expressed runs (calibration)

analysis_plan.mcnemar: exact binomial test on discordant pairs, b ~ Binomial(b+c, 0.5), one-sided
analysis_plan.no_optional_stopping: the diagnosis is a single pass; the sheet is hash-committed by the diagnostician before the answer key, the assignment, and the rule outputs are unsealed
analysis_plan.scorer: experiments/study_g_score.py, committed alongside this protocol before the corpus was generated; no scoring choice is made after data exist

thresholds_and_versions.instrument: HilbertBench v1.0.0 (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.21009245), thresholds frozen since Study E
thresholds_and_versions.rule: Study F decision rule, commit 5c25350, unchanged

relation_to_registrations: Registered as a SECOND registration on the existing OSF project (the Study E registration, DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/2PWHU, is immutable and untouched). This document and its commitments are published to the public repository before corpus generation; the OSF registration is filed before the diagnostician receives the corpus.
